claims.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
claims.evidence: For h(r)=min(2,r), a direct case split on whether each nonnegative operand is 0, 1, or at least 2 proves h(a+b)=h(h(a)+h(b)) and h(ab)=h(h(a)h(b)). Thus h is a homomorphism to the saturated semiring. All assignment and path counts in the transfer construction are formed using finite sums and products, so their saturated values remain exact as zero, one, or at least two. Those distinctions suffice for both uniqueness quantifiers and the outer existence test.
claims.search_method: Independent semiring proof, followed by exhaustive exact-integer checks of scalar identities and every 2-coordinate saturated vector times every 2-by-2 saturated matrix.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
claims.evidence: For fixed type-3 assignment x and type-2 assignment y, induction over columns gives q_i(γ)=h(number of type-1 prefix assignments taking initial carry 0 to γ). Hence the inner uniqueness condition is exactly q_m(α)=1. For fixed x, B_i aggregates local type-2 assignments by their deterministic map p↦pA_i; a second induction gives d_i(q)=h(number of type-2 prefixes producing q). Consequently the middle uniqueness condition is exactly that the saturated sum of d_m(q) over q with q(α)=1 equals 1. Layered reachability over local type-3 choices then implements the outer existential quantifier. Initial carry 0, fixed final carry α, and empty type blocks are handled correctly. If a column has a,b,c cells of types 3,2,1, then a+b+c≤3; constructing all local data examines O(n^(a+b+c))≤O(n^3) tuples. The 2, 3^2, and 3^9 state factors are constants, yielding O(m n^3) under the explicitly stated source convention. Exhaustive comparison with literal nested semantics passed all 31,250 base-2 two-column instances and all 432 base-3 one-column instances.
claims.search_method: Re-derived both transfer invariants and the running-time bound from the source model, then exhaustively compared the construction with direct nested-quantifier enumeration using exact integers.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this does not provide the requested meaningful matching hardness classification.
claims.evidence: Membership follows from the verified upper bound in the source convention. The language is nontrivial: fixed base-2 one-column YES and NO instances exist. For every L in P, a polynomial-time decider for L can output the fixed YES instance on members and the fixed NO instance otherwise, giving a polynomial-time many-one reduction. This is formally P-hard for that reduction notion and hence P-complete, but the same argument applies to every nontrivial language in P. It supplies no logspace P-hardness or other discriminating lower bound, so the claim correctly denies that it meets the target's meaningful matching-hardness requirement.
claims.witness: With base 2 and final carry 0, the one-column instance (type-3 blank)+0=0 is YES, while (type-3 blank)+1=0 is NO; the type-1 and type-2 blocks are empty in both instances.
claims.search_method: Applied the definition of polynomial-time many-one hardness and independently evaluated the fixed YES/NO instances under the literal level-3 quantifiers; both were also checked computationally.

claims.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
claims.evidence: Let S be the finite state set summarizing the already-eliminated lower tracks, with an acceptance subset encoding their nested uniqueness predicate. Eliminating the next globally unique track replaces a state by a saturated count vector in {0,1,2}^S. Local transitions sum over that track's local digits, and the new final predicate tests whether exactly one counted assignment reaches an accepting old state. The same columnwise induction used at level 3 proves this invariant at every lift. Starting from two carry states and repeating through types 1,...,k−1 produces a tower-sized but finite state set depending only on fixed k. Type-k digits remain ordinary local choices handled by layered reachability. Since each column contains at most three variable cells, local enumeration is polynomial under the source convention. Exact comparisons with literal semantics passed every one-column instance through level 5 in base 2 and through level 4 in base 3.
claims.search_method: Proved the iterated saturated-count lifting by induction on the number of unique tracks and implemented an independent generic lifting algorithm for exhaustive comparison with literal nested quantifiers.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for both a complete upper bound and a meaningful matching hardness classification. The draft rigorously establishes a polynomial-time upper bound for level 3 under the source paper's convention and also extends the construction to every fixed level. Its polynomial-time-many-one P-completeness observation is deliberately non-discriminating: the reduction decides the source P language itself and therefore does not constitute the requested meaningful matching lower bound. The final writeup explicitly acknowledges that omission and labels the resolution PARTIAL. Thus the draft makes material correct progress without resolving the entire target, and its claimed resolution is accurate rather than overstated or understated.

Derived the O(m n^3) bound from the three cells per column and constant saturated state spaces under the source convention.
